questions.def: "There is" introduces something singular that exists.
questions.question: ___ a cat on the roof.

questions.def: "There were" agrees with the plural noun "people".
questions.question: ___ many people at the party last night.

questions.def: Question form for plural "shops": "Are there".
questions.question: ___ any shops near your house?

questions.def: "There is" is used for singular, countable problems.
questions.question: ___ a problem with my computer.

questions.def: "There are" agrees with the plural noun "chairs".
questions.question: ___ enough chairs for everyone to sit down.

questions.def: Question form for singular "movie": "Is there".
questions.question: ___ a good movie on TV tonight?

questions.def: "There is" is used with uncountable nouns like "sugar".
questions.question: ___ no sugar in my tea.

questions.def: "There is" introduces a singular piece of information.
questions.question: I think ___ something I need to tell you.

questions.def: "There is" introduces singular "something".
questions.question: I think ___ something wrong here.

questions.def: "There is" is often used with uncountable nouns like "traffic".
questions.question: ___ a lot of traffic today.

questions.def: "There is" introduces a singular noun phrase "a good reason".
questions.question: ___ a good reason to be happy.

questions.def: Question form for plural noun "questions": "Are there".
questions.question: ___ any questions at the end of the class?

questions.def: "Is there" is the question form with singular noun.
questions.question: ___ a bus stop near my house?

questions.def: "There has been" is used with uncountable nouns like "rain".
questions.question: ___ a lot of rain this year.

questions.def: Question form: singular countable noun "message".
questions.question: ___ any message for me today?

questions.def: "There was" for singular noun "one".
questions.question: ___ no one at home when I called.

questions.def: "There have been" with plural countable noun "changes".
questions.question: ___ many changes in the city lately.

questions.def: Question form: uncountable noun "time".
questions.question: ___ enough time to finish?

questions.def: "There's" (There is) is used with singular nouns.
questions.question: ___ a reason why I'm late.

questions.def: "There are" agrees with plural noun "answers".
questions.question: ___ no easy answers to this question.

questions.def: Question form: singular noun "anything".
questions.question: ___ anything I can do to help?

questions.def: "There is" introduces a singular noun phrase.
questions.question: ___ a new restaurant in town.

questions.def: "There are" agrees with plural noun "articles".
questions.question: ___ some interesting articles in this newspaper.

questions.def: We use 'There is' to introduce a singular noun.
questions.question: ___ a cat sitting on the roof.

questions.def: 'Were there' is used to ask about plural nouns in the past.
questions.question: ___ many people at the party last night?

questions.def: We use 'There is' with uncountable nouns like 'milk'.
questions.question: ___ no milk in the fridge.

questions.def: 'There seems to be' introduces a possibility or an issue.
questions.question: ___ a problem with my computer.

questions.def: 'Is there' is the correct question form for singular nouns.
questions.question: ___ a bus stop near your house?

questions.def: 'There are' introduces plural nouns ('cars').
questions.question: ___ many cars on the road today.

questions.def: 'There is' is followed by a singular pronoun or noun phrase.
questions.question: ___ nothing I can do to help.
